name: Inkling
tagline: Apache on the tin, terms in the drawer
description: Thinking Machines Lab's first open-weights model: a 975B-total / 41B-active sparse MoE (6 of 256 experts plus 2 shared) that takes text, images, and audio in, with a 1M-token context, trained on 45T tokens. Day-0 support landed in transformers, vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp, with an NVFP4 checkpoint alongside BF16.
why: The most-watched debut of 2026 — Mira Murati's lab shipping trillion-scale weights with frontier-class scores (77.6% SWE-Bench Verified, 46.0% HLE with tools). But the Apache-2.0 label comes with a separately binding Model Acceptable Use Policy, which is exactly the kind of rider this site exists to flag.
useCases: Multimodal apps that need voice and vision in one model

setup.requirements: ~2TB VRAM for BF16, ~600GB for the NVFP4 build; community 1-bit GGUFs squeeze it far smaller at a real quality cost

license.weights: Apache-2.0 tag + binding Model Acceptable Use Policy
license.notes: The Hugging Face license tag reads Apache-2.0, but Thinking Machines' Model AUP states that by accessing, downloading, or using the model you agree to be bound by its use restrictions. A binding use-restriction rider fails OSD #6, so per house policy this is partial, not open — downgraded rather than rounded up. Flagged for review.

limitations: The hardware appetite is enormous, the AUP restricts fields of use, and this is a v1 with no stability track record — the card itself warns against unvalidated high-stakes deployment.
take: The year's biggest debut is also its best license quiz. Read past the tag before you build on it.
